2. The circumstances which led to this Rule may briefly be stated as follows:- The petitioner was the defendant No.2 in Other Suit No. 38 of 1984 and prayed for saham in respect of 87 acres of land. The plaintiff No. 2 took settlement of .40 acres of land from Plot No. 7990 by virtue of dakhila from its owner Ahmed Ali and possessed the same and that his name has duly been recorded in RS Khatian No. 79 and that the plaintiff No. 2. Has been paying rents for that land. The plaintiff-petitioner further took settlement of 1.21 acres of land from Ahmed Ali by virtue of dakhila from plot No. 3013 appertaining to CS Khatian No. 728 and his name has rightly been recorded in the RS Khatian and the plaintiff No. 2 has been paying usual rents. The original owner Ahmed Ali sold 0.27 acres of land from Plot No. 3033 to Tepamadhupur Awlia Madrasha by a registered kabala deed dated 18-3-1963 and gave delivery of possession of that land. That while said Madrasha possessing the land, its Secretary being authorised by the Madrasha Committee sold the same to the plaintiff No.2 by a kabala deed dated 6-4-1966 and has given delivery of possession. The plaintiff No.2 in this way in all has acquired 1.88 acres ofland. But due to mistake be could not claim that 1.88 acres of land but he claimed only 0.87 acres of land which was decreed in his favour in preliminary form. 

 13. On perusal of the impugned judgment and order it appears that the Court of trial below rejected the application for amendment dated 9-5-1992 only on the ground that the preliminary decree has already been drawn up and the suit is to be reopened giving due opportunities to the parties to re-call the witnesses already examined and to adduce further evidences which cause injustice to the other side. On a perusal of the application dated 9-5-1992 it appears that the poor illiterate plaintiff-petitioner though has been in possession of 1.88 acres of land excluding the decretal land .87 acres of land for which he paid separate court fees and have been in possession duly paying rents to the Government and his name was also recorded in RS Khatian is being deprived by the impugned order. It is well settled that rule 17 of Order XVIII empowers the Court to re-call at any stage a witness who has been examined and cross-examined. The powers under the rule are very wide and Court can re-call a witness even while considering its judgment, if any, ambiguity or omission is noticed. The power can be exercised suo motu and also at the instance of a party. On perusal of the application dated 9-5-1992 it appears to me that the amendment which the petitioner wanted to put to the said PWs after re-calling appears to be very much relevant and pertinent for determining the issues involved in the suit for an end to the litigation and the controversy in between the parties and thereby ends of justice will be met. In my opinion, the Court of trial below under misconception of law and facts rejected the said application without directing himself to the legal aspect of the case;it is also the settled principle of law that a suit for partition remains pending till passing of the final decree. There would be obviously no bar to the Court taking any further steps which it could have taken before the preliminary decree. I, therefore, find no merit in the contention raised by Mr Mahmudul Islam, learned Senior Advocate, appearing on behalf of the defendant-opposite parties, on the ground that as long as a suit is pending a relief cannot be refused.
